prompt_en: An understated natural photograph records a quiet moment in which firelight visibly affects an inhabited room. In a rain-dark boarding-house common room during a brief winter power cut, a living fire burns inside a low open firebox in a continuous raised masonry cooking platform. The brickwork wraps continuously around the low wood opening, while a cast-iron kettle nests in the platform directly over that same burning cavity. The kettle seating rim and the open fuel mouth remain visible together, making the hot-drink source part of the same domestic hearth that warms her. Two partially charred split logs rest on a grate over gray ash; small yellow-orange flame tongues rise from their darkened edges, with separate dull-red embers underneath. A faint smoke thread rises inside the blackened firebox toward the throat of the chimney. The woman follows the reference image's facial proportions, black bob and wispy bangs; the reference guides her face and hair. Seated on a low wooden bench outside the raised hearth, she steadies a blue ceramic cup upright between both hands in her lap, with elbows resting on her thighs and both shoes on the floor. Her head turns slightly toward the fire. Her slightly parted lips and settling shoulders suggest the first comfortable exhale after a wet walk. A pale knitted cardigan over a washed charcoal dress and the soft firelit contour of her cheek make her presence quietly appealing in this ordinary pause. A folded damp wool scarf rests beside her, and faint wet boot prints lead from the doorway across worn terracotta tile. A raincoat hangs above a brass umbrella tray. Thin tea vapor rises locally from the cup and dissolves above her hands, spatially separate from the smoke inside the firebox. Warm light strikes her near cheek and hands, puts an orange edge on the brass tray, and repeats as small reflections in wet tile close to the hearth; cool blue dusk rests in the rain-streaked window glass. The unlit ceiling bulbs stay dark while the room gathers around the hearth's glow. Use a landscape medium-wide frame at seated eye level from a front three-quarter view, with the face, both cup-holding hands, burning logs and nearby floor connected within the image. A natural 50mm perspective and moderate depth of field retain the material relationships, readable flame edges, lived-in wood and stone, and natural skin texture. The photograph feels observed during a private pause, with restrained grain and balanced highlights.
